messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Skyline Analytics

Hi Priya,

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and the next steps we discussed so everyone is aligned. If I missed anything, please call it out.

Pain points
- Production latency variability during peak batch jobs and unpredictable token costs.
- Need for strict data isolation and auditability for regulated customers.
- Current system (self-hosted instances on AWS) struggles to hit predictable TPS for real-time features.

Current stack (as described)
- Inference today: EC2 g4dn-based fleet with a custom batching proxy
- Model infra: internal LLMs (distilled) + a small use of hosted models for spikes
- Observability: Grafana + internal logging; limited token-level cost attribution

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable throughput: 150-250 TPS sustained for real-time endpoints, with headroom for 2x burst
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 120ms for short-context requests
- Strong isolation: tenant-level segregation with customer-only GPU pools and encrypted KV caches
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and auditable access logs

Sizing / autoscaling notes (initial estimate)
- Recommend reserved pool footprint to cover baseline 150 TPS (we'll size precisely after metrics review)
- Autoscaling/burst policy: allow 2x burst capacity for short windows (5-15 minutes) with automated fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained

Next steps
1) Marissa (SE) to run a quick technical deep-dive and workload profiling with your infra team, target next Wed 6/16.
2) David (Infra) to review network & security requirements (VPC peering, egress rules, KMS).
3) Priya to share recent production QPS sample + token distribution (attach CSV if possible).
4) We'll send an initial commercial estimate and a proposed PoC plan (2-3/4 week reserved pool trial).

Attachments: Skyline_Specs.pdf (you mentioned a traffic sample), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Thanks, Rafael

Rafael Mendes
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Priya Shah <priya@skyline.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Skyline Analytics

Thanks Rafael, this looks good and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 150-250 TPS target is for our core recommendation endpoint; we also have a lower-priority batch scoring job that can tolerate higher latency but spikes nightly.
- For isolation, we need tenant-level encryption keys and the ability to rotate keys on a per-customer basis (SOC/compliance requirement).
- Current production QPS sample: attaching nightly_traffic_sample.csv (see attached).

Can you confirm if the reserved pool option supports per-tenant KMS integration and whether you support private VPC deployment (we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints)?

Also, procurement wants a ballpark number for a 2-month PoC (we can consider credits vs. short-term commit). Hope we can keep commercials flexible for a trial.

On the schedule, 6/16 works for the technical deep-dive; please include Marissa and David.

Best,
Priya
Head of ML Infrastructure | Skyline Analytics
priya@skyline.ai | +1 650-555-0110

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Priya, glad 6/16 works. A few follow-ups and confirmations before the deep-dive:

- Per-tenant KMS: yes — we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll include config details in the SE deep-dive.
- VPC options: we support VPC peering for Redwood Private (customer VPC + private control plane). For Hosted Dedicated, we offer private endpoints and VPC peering on enterprise plans, Marissa will outline the network options.
- PoC commercials: we'll propose a 2-month PoC estimate that minimizes upfront commitment (mix of credits + short reserved commitment). I'll include a ballpark in the commercial note later this week.

Proposed technical deep-dive agenda (30-45m):
1) Workload profiling & metrics review (you + our infra) — goals: confirm TPS distribution and sizing
2) Network/security & KMS walk-through (David + Marissa)
3) Autoscaling & fallback policy discussion (how we handle bursts and model variants)
4) PoC plan & success criteria (what we measure during the trial)

Tentative sizing (initial rough):
- Baseline reserved pool sized for ~150 TPS sustained; configured with autoscale headroom to ~300 TPS for 10-15 minute bursts.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools per customer + network-level segregation.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown + per-route latency dashboards (we will provision access for your SREs during PoC).

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: will send a calendar invite for 6/16 with a short profiling template for the traffic sample.
- Priya: please attach the nightly_traffic_sample.csv to the HubSpot deal (or share via secure link).
- Rafael: I'll follow up with a PoC commercial outline and a DocuSign link for a short NDA/PoC MOU if you want to accelerate.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Thanks, Rafael
